# Maintainer draft: clean-clone-quickstart

# Clean-clone maintainer audit

**Scope:** Read-only review of five pinned files, not a fresh clone, installation, test or replay. References [1]–[5] map to citations below. This runbook requires maintainer review before publication.

## Ordered runbook

1. **Prepare.** Use Git, Node.js >=22 with npm, and Python >=3.9 on PATH. Check `git --version`, `node --version`, `npm --version`, and `python3 --version`. Runtime OPA installation supports macOS/Linux arm64/x64; Windows is not a qualified CI target. No OSuite account or GitHub credential is needed for offline work. “Offline-first” means no provider writes: initial acquisition still downloads source, npm packages and OPA unless verified dependencies are already available. [1,2]

2. **Acquire and pin, from a new parent directory.** The following are proposed commands, not commands executed in this audit. Keep lowercase sibling directories:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Spec.git action-effect-spec
git clone https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench.git action-effect-bench
cd action-effect-bench
git checkout --detach cecde389637be4f5fd3482e4942ce3fd1a623ac6
git -C ../action-effect-spec checkout --detach "$(node -p "require('./spec-lock.json').commit")"
git rev-parse HEAD
git -C ../action-effect-spec rev-parse HEAD
git status --short
git -C ../action-effect-spec status --short
```

Require Bench `cecde389637be4f5fd3482e4942ce3fd1a623ac6` and Spec `a9b86f4b529a5e330c2a9bf1b8c4c259a7b36e40`, with no unexplained source changes. This pins the supplied audit snapshot; release-tag resolution was not independently inspected. Layout is `parent/{action-effect-bench,action-effect-spec}`. **All commands below use the Bench root**, except the explicitly marked original-corpus subshell. Pin Bench before reading its lock; do not substitute latest Spec. [1,2,4]

3. **Install, then gate readiness.**

```sh
npm ci --prefix runtime-pilot --ignore-scripts --no-fund --no-audit
node runtime-pilot/install-tools.mjs
```

Require successful completion of both before runtime tests or replay. Quickstart states dependency-lock pins of MCP SDK 1.32.1 and Octokit REST 22.0.1; the package lock itself was not an allowed source, so these pins were not independently inspected. Require actual OPA 1.21.2 and installer verification against the matching platform entry in `runtime-pilot/tools.json`, not a version string alone. The manifest has four distinct hashes: do not apply the historical macOS-arm64 cache hash to other platforms. [1,5]

**On setup failure:** stop runtime evaluation, retain logs/nonzero exits and any reports already produced. Restore download availability or supply a matching cached executable and require unchanged installer verification. Never use a stub or disable checksum/TLS checks. Cache destination/mechanics are not established by these sources; obtain maintainer guidance rather than inventing a bypass. Without verified dependencies, report setup blocked, not test failure or successful reproduction. [1,3]

4. **Run offline runtime checks, stopping on failures.**

```sh
node --test runtime-pilot/tests/*.test.mjs
python3 -B -W error -m unittest discover -s runtime-pilot/tests -p 'test_*.py'
node runtime-pilot/offline-run.mjs
node runtime-pilot/replay.mjs reports/runtime-pilot-offline-2026-10-19T04-23-54.715Z-6bb423.json
```

Retain each new report JSON and adjacent `.sha256`, including unsuccessful attempts. Replay checks integrity, inputs, source identity, mapping and OPA decisions, not original timing. On source/checksum mismatch, stop; use the report's recorded source revision in a separate reproduction checkout, with its own lock. Do not edit evidence or overwrite failures with a passing rerun. [1]

5. **Optionally reproduce the original corpus.** No npm dependencies are needed for this separate path. This subshell changes to the sibling parent and returns to Bench afterward: [2]

```sh
(
cd ..
node action-effect-bench/conformance/case-source.mjs --check &&
node --test action-effect-spec/implementations/javascript/*.test.mjs action-effect-bench/conformance/runner.test.mjs action-effect-bench/conformance/entrypoints.test.mjs &&
python3 -B -W error -m unittest discover -s action-effect-spec/implementations/python/tests &&
node action-effect-bench/conformance/run.mjs
)
```

## Published verification, not current execution

[3] reports Linux Node 22/Python 3.11 and macOS Node 24/Python 3.13 CI success: dependency/verified OPA installation, tests, original 102-case comparison and new offline runtime comparison, without live credentials or comments.

Its separate public clone used Bench `ede12ea`, pinned Spec, and runtime inventory identical to measured implementation `9f638df994504ba6f5d82c0b5409922a0be7a72e`. OPA download timed out; prematurely started replay returned `valid:false`, and an incomplete test process was stopped. These retained setup failures preceded hash-verified cached OPA use—not a second successful fresh local download.

After setup, reported passes were 75 original JS/harness, 115 Spec Python, 333 runtime JS and 50 runtime Python methods; original consumers and agreement were 102/102 with zero adapter faults. Offline replay validated 216 rows plus 52 diagnostic/reference records. Live replay validated 32 rows and 12 anonymous readbacks, with no new POST. Linked raw reports and CI logs were not inspected; these are the published account, not independent validation. [3]

## Live boundary and disposition

Offline commands above neither need credentials nor post comments. Optional replay `--github` adds network GETs and time-dependent current-content evidence, not historical causality. Live posting needs separate owner authorization, a fresh dedicated issue, narrow `gh` credentials and agreed limits; never reuse issue #1 or retry uncertain POSTs. [1,3]

**Clarification warranted:** add the Bench checkout pin before reading the Spec lock, and an explicit “STOP until npm and verified OPA setup succeed” gate before tests/replay. Explain initial network/cache needs and document verified-cache placement. Also distinguish release tag `v0.2.0-draft.1` from lock field `spec_version: 0.1.0-draft.1`; confirm its intended meaning rather than silently changing the pin. [1–5]

## Conclusion
The offline-first path is documented, but checkout identity and dependency-readiness gates need precise clarification. Published verification retains setup failures and successful post-cache checks; this audit only read pinned sources and did not reproduce those results. Maintainer review is required before publication.

2. https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/blob/cecde389637be4f5fd3482e4942ce3fd1a623ac6/README.md

4. https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/blob/cecde389637be4f5fd3482e4942ce3fd1a623ac6/spec-lock.json
5. https://github.com/OndCo/Action-Effect-Bench/blob/cecde389637be4f5fd3482e4942ce3fd1a623ac6/runtime-pilot/tools.json

# Consumer v1 → v1.1 migration note

**Draft for maintainer review before publication.** Based on the three pinned sources [1–3]; this task read documentation, not implementation code or deployments.

## Identity and compatibility

The change-record heading `0.2.0-draft.1` is a release identity, not the core wire version. Processing contract `offline-consumer-v1.1` is opt-in; core `spec_version` stays `0.1.0-draft.1`. The refund domain profile remains `https://example.org/profiles/refund/0.1.0-draft.1`, with canonical manifest SHA-256 `dddac40519b57620ca8b6fec558746ed8fb1f6ddf77263fd93cf5b2b582f2e00`. The separately added GitHub issue-comment profile does not make refund consumers understand GitHub. [2,3]

| Surface | Existing/default v1 clients | Opt-in v1.1 |
|---|---|---|
| Selection | Omission or explicit `offline-consumer-v1` preserves behavior/output | Explicit startup selection required |
| `hello` | No new field | Adds only `contract: offline-consumer-v1.1` to result |
| Configuration | Legacy rules retained, including JS nullish fallback | Explicit invalid configuration rejected before frames |
| Final-domain errors | Frozen v1 behavior | Ordered applicability → cardinality → missing amount → coupled projection |
| Wire/domain | Existing versions and bindings | Unchanged; seven frozen files unchanged |
| Adapter/results | Existing framing and rejection continuation | Unchanged `check`/`canonicalize` shapes, digests, limits |
| Meaning/scope | Offline partial declaration, no authority | Unchanged; no new domain, network, cache or authorization |

## Adoption and rollback

Use Node >=22 or Python >=3.9; entry points work from any current directory. Start either:

```sh
node implementations/javascript/cli.mjs --contract offline-consumer-v1.1 --basis PATH
python3 implementations/python/cli.py --contract offline-consumer-v1.1 --basis PATH
```

`--basis` and `--contract` may appear in either order. Omit basis to use bundled `examples/synthetic-basis.json`; it is loaded once as a startup snapshot. Unknown, empty, missing-value or repeated contract options are fatal startup errors, not fallback or per-document `unsupported_profile` results. [1,2]

API selection:

```javascript
const options = { contract: 'offline-consumer-v1.1' };
const check = createConsumer(options); // optional basis/profile
capabilities(options);
handleFrame(frameBytes, check, options); // propagate options for hello
```
```python
consumer = Consumer(load_snapshot(basis_path), contract="offline-consumer-v1.1")
consumer.hello()
consumer.check(document_bytes)
```

Unsupported contracts/unusable configuration raise startup exceptions. Omitted API contracts select v1; JS `undefined` contract also means omitted, but explicit null/non-string contracts are invalid. Legacy class-level Python `Consumer.hello()` still reports v1. Roll back by restarting/recreating consumers with omitted contract or explicit `offline-consumer-v1`, consistently updating JS hello options and retaining the intended basis. Rollback selects processing behavior, not a different wire version/profile. [2]

Only the launcher configures trust. Never add `contract` to request or document: these extra fields remain invalid. Requests cannot change fixtures, refresh state, fetch references or grant authority. [1,2]

## Externally visible behavior

- **Capabilities:** v1.1 keeps `capabilities/offline_snapshot`, `authority: not_evaluated`, unchanged wire/profile identifiers, `numeric_domain: safe_integer_tokens_only`, and `acceptance_cache: false`; the adapter still wraps the result with request ID. Only its contract member is new. [2]
- **Startup failures:** unreadable files; invalid encoding/JSON, duplicate keys or Unicode; startup size/depth/numeric-subset violations; nonmatching full canonical manifest; or a nonobject basis/missing or nonobject `input`, `implementation`, `context`, `mapping`, `declaration` fail before serving. CLI exits nonzero, emits no stdout (not even hello), and uses fixed stderr diagnostics without contents, argument values, paths, secrets or stacks. API exceptions must not embed configuration contents. Explicit null basis is invalid; JS explicit undefined basis/profile is also invalid rather than defaulting. [2]
- **Applicability:** the five required objects may be empty at startup. Unsupported nested scalar values load but fail final applicability. Only absent `amount_minor` permits unknown amount; a present value must be an exact decimal integer string in 0..999999999999. Null, numeric values, signs, leading zeros and other invalid representations do not become unknowns. [2]
- **Precedence:** stages 1–9 remain first: syntax/limits, numeric support, version/structure, references, critical extensions, profile binding, evidence scope and artifact binding. Thus stale invocation digest beats bad fixture currency; malformed evidence source fails structure, and issuer mismatch fails artifact binding before applicability. [1,2]
- **Stage 10:** bad fixture → `untrusted_evidence/applicability`; then zero/multiple effects → `untrusted_evidence/effect_projection`; then missing both named amount and exact targeted unknown → `invalid_input/structure`; then remaining coupled projection defects → `untrusted_evidence/effect_projection`. Represented wrong values/units/scales belong to the last class. Earlier reference errors still win. Success remains `accepted_partial/declared_partial`, with digest and counts, never truth, permission, observation or a checked bound. [2]

## Verification and evidence

**Pending locally for both languages:**
```sh
node --test implementations/javascript/*.test.mjs
python3 -B -W error -m unittest discover -s implementations/python/tests
```

- Check default/explicit v1 parity, v1.1 hello and API option propagation; startup option failures and redaction; omitted versus explicit null/undefined configuration.
- Check invalid startup shapes versus valid-shape inapplicable fixtures; earlier-stage precedence; every paired final-stage defect, repairing the higher-priority defect to expose the lower one. Verify unchanged framing, continuation, canonicalization, digests and rollback.
- Keep frozen v1 corpus explicitly on v1; record runtimes/source/case hashes and expected-result matches separately from cross-language agreement. Agreement alone is not correctness. [1,2]

**Historical only:** sources report both suites discovered in CI and added paired-defect/legacy tests. The changelog records a JS symlink-entry repair and regression failing before the fix; Python and semantic evaluation were unchanged. Earlier benchmark reports remain tied to their snapshots. [2,3]

**Current evidence:** three successful pinned GitHub reads via SDK/REST. No startup observed, tests executed, CI inspected, customer deployments checked, writes made or authorization obtained. Implementation/test artifacts and fresh outcomes were unavailable in the supplied sources. These are same-project tests, not external validation, certification or full core conformance.

## Conclusion
Adopt v1.1 only through explicit startup selection after maintainer review and local JavaScript/Python verification. Preserve default v1 clients and roll back by restoring v1 selection; neither migration nor rollback changes the core wire version or refund profile binding.

# Official GitHub MCP compatibility assessment

## Identity and provenance

Source keys [1]–[5] refer to the exact pinned URLs in `citations`, in order.

| Layer | Identity supported by sources | Boundary |

| Dependency | Private ESM package `action-effect-runtime-pilot@0.2.0-draft.1`, Node `>=22`; declares `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.1`, `@octokit/rest@22.0.1`, `ajv@8.20.0`, `zod@4.6.7` [2] | Official MCP SDK use is not official GitHub server use. Declaration alone does not verify installed bytes. |
| Server implementation | Source constructs `McpServer` named `action-effect-comment-pilot`, version `0.2.0-draft.1` [1] | A custom pilot server, not evidence of the official GitHub MCP implementation. |
| Transport | Imports `StdioServerTransport` and connects it; README describes real SDK stdio initialize/list/call exchanges [1,3] | No hosted/HTTP transport or remote authentication flow is established. |
| Declared profile binding | GitHub Issue Comment Profile 1 requires `context.implementation = "github-comment-bridge/1"`; identity preimage has `kind: "declaration"` [4] | Neither server name nor SDK version; not binary attestation or proof of GitHub internals. Profile release is `v0.2.0-draft.1`, core wire version remains `0.1.0-draft.1`. |

The current runner separately reports a local stdio process named `github-mcp-server@2.0.2`, executable SHA-256 `2d431e46617f06b1516818fa09917096ff6dfc3664b37b0bdb31e1c1a35be368`, startup observed, negotiated protocol `2025-11-25`. All five source reads succeeded on the MCP lane. This establishes current public-read activity under that reported execution identity, not official provenance of that executable or execution of the historical pilot.

## Released interface

The pilot registers one tool, **`add_issue_comment`**. Its advertised input is a strict object with required `owner: string`, `repo: string`, `issue_number: integer`, `body: string`; extra keys are rejected. Server input-element limit is 32. Annotations are `readOnlyHint:false`, `destructiveHint:false`, `idempotentHint:false`, `openWorldHint:true` [1]. These hints do not grant permission.

The profile adds narrower acceptance rules than the Zod schema alone [4]:
- Owner: `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}`; repo: `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,100}`, excluding `.` and `..`.
- Issue: positive integer through 2147483647, not a boolean. Body: nonempty Unicode-scalar string, at most 8192 exact UTF-8 bytes.
- Only specified keys; no normalization, path unescaping, URL resolution, templates or caller endpoints. Only creation via `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/issues/issue_number/comments`; updates, deletes and arbitrary tools are outside scope.
- Nonempty configured principal and data class plus the exact implementation binding are required. Missing/wrong binding is untrusted evidence. Live demonstrations are restricted to authorized synthetic-public resources; profile acceptance is not authorization.

The handler captures `{lane:"mcp",call:{name:"add_issue_comment",arguments:args}}`; this is a local capture envelope, not a replacement for MCP `tools/call` [1,4]. Configuration accepts `offline-map` or `live` and `protocol` or `structured`. Offline calls prepare; live calls delegate execution to the gate/provider. Optional lost-ack injection discards a successful create acknowledgment and adds fault information [1].

Response representation is **`{content:[{type:"text",text:JSON.stringify(result)}]}`**: JSON serialized inside an MCP text block, not a declared structured-output schema or a proven official-server response format [1]. Profile acceptance is `accepted_partial/declared_partial`, with `authority:not_evaluated`, description digest and checked projection. Processing status, policy decision and provider outcome are distinct [3,4]. The imported gate/provider implementations were not supplied, so their complete result contract was not inspected.

## Supported versus unverified

**Supported:** a bounded custom MCP/SDK bridge, stdio wiring, explicit comment-input mapping and declared profile identity. The release documentation reports 32 matching planned live checks, 12 public comments, four read-only lost-ack recoveries and four suppressed duplicates [5]. These are historical same-project claims, not runs observed here; the README bounds them to eight scripted scenarios across two lanes and two strategies [3].

**Unverified:** compatibility with an identified official GitHub MCP server revision, its actual tool schema, response/error semantics, transport configurations or authentication. No official implementation source, tool-list capture, interoperability trace or installed dependency evidence was supplied. Matching a tool name or using the official SDK cannot close those gaps. No mutation, pilot test, remote authentication experiment, certification or customer deployment check occurred in this task.

## Maintainer disposition / next checks

1. Document now: “Custom stdio MCP pilot using the official MCP SDK; official GitHub MCP interoperability not yet validated.” Require maintainer review before publication.
2. Pin the intended official repository/release and executable provenance; retain its initialize and `tools/list` evidence. Compare exact required fields, validation, annotations, capabilities and protocol/transport versions.
3. Define an adapter for result/error representation and capture at the actual dispatch boundary. Test profile restrictions and negative cases; do not relabel the declaration as attestation.
4. Separately plan authorized sandbox checks of provider identity, credential scope, policy enforcement, one comment/readback and uncertain-delivery handling. Retain traces and distinguish offline mapping from real dispatch. Do not infer setup or permission from this report.
5. If hosted transport is intended, validate its authentication separately. Keep non-claims for downstream effects, global exactly-once delivery and production qualification [3–5].

## Conclusion
The sources establish a custom stdio MCP pilot built with the official MCP SDK, not validated integration with the official GitHub MCP implementation. Current successful public reads and historical release-reported live results are distinct evidence. Stronger interoperability claims need pinned official-server provenance, schema/response comparison and separately authorized integration observations; maintainer review is required before publication.

## Keep the evidence populations separate

- **Design:** 40 CORE scenarios [1]; a separate 12-case broader development design index [5]. Neither is an additional executed suite. The requirements' drafting-time nonexecution statement is consistent with later, differently scoped measurements.
- **Offline development:** 80 frozen same-project cases with contract-derived expectations authored before candidate inspection; 22 regressions authored after defects were found [2,5]. Preserve both denominators even when reporting 102 total.
- **Unit methods:** [4] reports 64 Spec JavaScript + 115 Spec Python + 11 legacy harness + 333 runtime JavaScript + 50 runtime Python = **573 methods**. These are not 573 benchmark workloads or SaaS effects. Harness fixture workers exercise faults, not consumer experiments. Eight runtime gate regressions failed before correction and passed afterward; do not add them as live incidents.
- **Runtime development:** 55 authored cases, 22 base intents, 108 lane instances (53 SDK, 55 MCP) per path; 216 candidate rows across two paths. - **Reference / diagnostic:** 26/26 OPA reference-projection labels came from a separate same-project authoring path. A lossy ablation matched decisions 26/26 despite mapping 0/26: decision agreement can mask mapping errors [4].

# Conformance support statement

**Disposition: retain the bounded claims; no source correction is justified by these five files. Maintainer review is required before publication.** This review read pinned public documentation, not implementations, raw reports or CI logs. Measurements below are attributed release results, not tests performed here. References [1]–[5] follow the citations array.

## Claim-to-evidence crosswalk

| Contract / claim | Evidence | Actual supported scope |
|---|---|---|
| CORE-001–028 obligations | Requirements [1] | 40 designed scenarios: V01–V28 seed clauses plus V29–V40 adversarial additions. Not executable conformance evidence or exhaustive branch coverage; mandatory obligations cannot be waived into full conformance. |
| `offline-consumer-v1`, synthetic refund | Runner guide [2], release summary [4], README [5] | Reported 102/102 expected outputs per consumer, 102/102 agreement, zero adapter faults. Denominator is 80 public development cases plus 22 exposed post-review regressions, not 102 independent holdouts. No refund execution or authority evaluation. |
| Oracle and harness scope | [2], [5] | Expected status/reason, supported canonical bytes and selected scalar fields; response-contract and diagnostic digest checks. Accepted-description full digests are cross-compared, not independently supplied by a full-document oracle. Literal canonical vectors provide narrower byte-rule checks. Agreement is not independent correctness. |
| Opt-in `offline-consumer-v1.1` | Consumer contract [3] | Designed startup validation, sanitized fatal errors and final-stage precedence: applicability, cardinality, missing amount, remaining projection. Earlier stages retain priority. CLI/API opt-in leaves default v1, wire version and refund profile unchanged. Language-local regression tests and CI discovery are described; no separate v1.1 benchmark denominator is supplied here. The 102-case v1 result must not be relabeled v1.1. |
| Bounded GitHub-comment runtime | Release summary [4], README [5] | Historical protocol and structured-baseline paths share OPA, ledger and dispatcher. Reported mapping, authorization and provider observations concern direct issue comments, not arbitrary programs, complete descendants or a general production gateway. This is separate from offline refund support. |
| Platform / operational readiness | [4], [5] | Reported Linux/macOS CI qualification; Windows is not qualified. Zero externally independently authored evaluations. No certification, protected study or production SLA. |

## Keep the evidence populations separate

- **Design:** 40 CORE scenarios [1]; a separate 12-case broader development design index [5]. Neither is an additional executed suite. The requirements' drafting-time nonexecution statement is consistent with later, differently scoped measurements.
- **Offline development:** 80 frozen same-project cases with contract-derived expectations authored before candidate inspection; 22 regressions authored after defects were found [2,5]. Preserve both denominators even when reporting 102 total.
- **Unit methods:** [4] reports 64 Spec JavaScript + 115 Spec Python + 11 legacy harness + 333 runtime JavaScript + 50 runtime Python = **573 methods**. These are not 573 benchmark workloads or SaaS effects. Harness fixture workers exercise faults, not consumer experiments. Eight runtime gate regressions failed before correction and passed afterward; do not add them as live incidents.
- **Runtime development:** 55 authored cases, 22 base intents, 108 lane instances (53 SDK, 55 MCP) per path; 216 candidate rows across two paths. Each path reports 108/108 mapping checks and 52/52 accepted-input authorization checks (22 allow, 28 deny, 2 review). The remaining 56 instances test nonacceptance. Cases were frozen before execution, not before implementation [4,5].
- **Reference / diagnostic:** 26/26 OPA reference-projection labels came from a separate same-project authoring path. A lossy ablation matched decisions 26/26 despite mapping 0/26: decision agreement can mask mapping errors [4].
- **Historical live:** Eight scripted scenarios × two paths × two lanes gave 32/32 planned checks and 12 new comments. Four comments followed deliberately injected acknowledgment loss and read-only recovery, without resend. Single-writer markers limit attribution; neither causality nor global exactly-once delivery is established. Timing is descriptive, not a speed claim [4].

## Proposed adopter-facing wording

> This draft offers two separately written offline refund consumers and a bounded GitHub-comment runtime example. Published same-project results demonstrate the specified outcomes on exposed development and regression inputs, not full CORE conformance or independent correctness. Offline acceptance is `accepted_partial/declared_partial` with `authority: not_evaluated`: it is not permission, observed execution or a checked descendant bound. Opt-in v1.1 hardens processing behavior without converting v1 corpus results into v1.1 evidence.
>
> Failures are retained: an initial runtime offline attempt failed scorer/adapter checks, and a setup attempt failed before successful verification. Those failures are not erased by later passes. Expected rejection is not an operational failure; crashes, malformed output and timeouts are adapter faults, not successful security blocks. Invalid live policy configuration was evaluation failure, not semantic denial. Unsupported contracts fail startup; unsupported fixture applicability in v1.1 yields the specified nonacceptance. Untested or unqualified domains, Windows, external evaluation, full descendants and production operations must not be described as demonstrated support.

## Maintainer action

Retain the existing scope warnings and separate denominators. No inconsistency warrants a file correction. Before stronger claims, inspect the linked raw reports and CI evidence, reproduce pinned suites, and enumerate failures/unsupported/skipped obligations. These artifacts, the base v1 contract and implementations were outside the supplied reads. Add separately labeled v1.1 execution evidence and independent full-digest oracles; full CORE claims require executable positive/negative vectors and independent consumers. Current successful MCP stdio reads are not a rerun of the historical SDK/MCP pilot, a hosted authentication test, authorization or customer-deployment verification.

## Conclusion
The supplied sources support a bounded, same-project development support statement, not full CORE conformance or independent correctness. Retain existing wording and evidence boundaries; no file correction is justified. Stronger claims require additional execution and independent evidence, and publication requires maintainer review.
